<!-- pr-reviewer: ab2f318f06468fe82935f58b2418f49ab6c76963 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

This is a safety-tier review. The PR lets three kinds generate G-code in an aligned setup.

### What looks good

- `verified_kind` adds only 2D Offset, Trace and Engrave. The tilt refusal and the non-mill refusal do not change.
- 2D Offset takes its whole-model region from `area::whole_model_pocket`. Pocket and 2D Adaptive use the same function, and #2210 verified it.
- Trace and Engrave take their region from `region_for_job` with `m_gen`. The material comes from `setup_align::facets_in`, so it is in the setup frame. The `Mark` depth law reads the same `m_gen.facets`.
- The new suite compares the turned part with the baked part on a turn about two axes. It compares moves (to 1e-6), the posted program, the post-blocking warnings and the stock simulation. It also proves that the model frame gives a different path.
- The decision file gives a reason for each kind that stays refused. Slot and Probe read the model frame, so the refusal is correct for them.
- The new test file is in the correct crate. It has a provenance line and a gate map.
- The body has `Changelog:` and `Refs #2276` (a partial fix). No goldens, snapshot PNGs, UI or process files change.

### Results (merged with main `3701b32d8`, built locally)

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `setup_align_2d_kinds` | 4 passed |
| `setup_align` | 10 passed |
| `opframe_picks` | 4 passed |
| `setup_align_2d_area` | 5 passed |
| `setup_align_3d` | 6 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib` + the three touched test targets, `-D warnings` | clean |

### Mutations (run by the reviewer, then reverted)

1. In `area::whole_model_pocket`, I changed the part facets to the model frame (`model::world_facets`). Result: `turned_offset2d_cuts_like_the_baked_part` fails at the gouge check. **Red.**
2. In `job.rs`, I changed the material of Trace and Engrave to the model-frame facets. Result: `turned_trace_cuts_like_the_baked_part` and `turned_engrave_cuts_like_the_baked_part` fail. **Red.**

Note: my first try of mutation 1 changed `material_of(world, setup, src)` to `material_of(world, None, src)`. The tests stayed green. This is correct behavior, because `None` gives the active setup, which is the same setup here. It is not a gap in the tests.

### Requested before merge

None.

### Notes (not blocking)

- `crates/app/src/setup_align.rs` is 408 lines. It was 406 lines on main, so it was already over the 400-line limit. A split can come later.
- The PR does not test Trace and Engrave with a picked chain as the source. The body says so. That path goes through `selection_region` with the setup, which #2210 pins for the pocket kinds.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: ab2f318f06468fe82935f58b2418f49ab6c76963 -->

**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**

- The change is small and at the right door. `verified_kind` adds exactly three kinds: 2D Offset, Trace and Engrave. `generation_problem` is read once, in `collect_job`, so every surface (GUI, MCP, CLI) takes the same answer. The MCP `generate` tool runs the same undoable `GenerateOperation` command, so this refusal change is visible through MCP with no new tool.
- The machine refusal, the tilt refusal and the unaligned fast path are untouched.
- The new suite proves the law on a turned part: 90 degrees about X, then 90 degrees about Z. Each kind cuts and posts the same program as the same part with the turn baked into its mesh, to 1e-6, and a different path than the part as modelled. The stock simulation asserts no gouge, and no warning blocks the post.
- The refusal side stays pinned: `kinds_without_proof_stay_refused_in_a_turned_setup` holds Slot and Drill refused by name, and the two updated tests hold Circular refused. The decision file names each kept refusal with its reason.
- No `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!` was added to source paths. The src change is one `matches!` arm and the refusal text.

**Results** (built locally in a review worktree; trial merge with main `4e0b9abef` was a clean fast-forward; the CRLF check showed no line-ending noise)

| Suite (camcraft-app) | Result |
|---|---|
| lib | 356 passed, 1 ignored |
| setup_align | 10 passed |
| setup_align_2d_kinds | 4 passed |
| setup_align_2d_area | 5 passed |
| setup_align_3d | 6 passed |
| opframe_picks | 4 passed |
| opframe_seam | 8 passed |
| fixture_locate_stock | 3 passed |
| heights_fixtures | 8 passed |
| setup_carry | 9 passed |
| stock_source_verdict | 22 passed |

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. UI and post processors are not touched; no golden or snapshot files changed.

**Requested before merge**

- None.

**Notes (not blocking)**

- `crates/app/src/setup_align.rs` is now 408 lines. The 400-line rule asks for a split along the domain seam when the next change grows it again.
- The body is honest about the gaps: area controls on 2D Offset and a picked-chain source for Trace and Engrave are not exercised in a turned setup. The second PR for the other kinds can extend the same helper calls to close them.
- The commit ends with `Refs #2276`, which is right for part 1; the issue stays open for the other kinds.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
